title: Trace operational journal: sampling heuristics & dashboard pruning — 2026-10-14
content:
Sprint week notes (standup cadence, experiments, and follow-ups)

Date: 2026-10-14
Owners on call: Anika (notes), Marcus (sampling infra), Leah (dashboards), Omar (cost telemetry)
Attendees: Anika Patel, Marcus Chen, Leah Rodriguez, Omar Siddiqi, Priya Nair (SRE), Tomás García (serving-runtime)

Purpose: capture the small-run experiments and operational changes we rolled this week to reduce trace volume and central dashboard noise while preserving SLO-relevant signal. This is a working log — items are deliberately terse.

Summary highlights:
- Rolled a proof-of-concept sampling policy for model-endpoint spans (endpoint-level rules + adaptive rate) to staging on 2026-10-12. Observed 18% reduction in raw span count for text-gen heavy endpoints without missing >1% of error traces.
- Dashboard pruning pass: removed 14 low-usage panels from the central "model-endpoints" dashboard, replaced two noisy panels with sampled percentile views. Expected cost delta: -6% in storage and query cost for that dashboard shard.
- Cost telemetry tweak: enabled coarse-grain aggregation for slow-query tracing in the EU region to reduce export cardinality.

Standup log (timed bullets)
- 09:10 - Marcus: sampling policy rollout notes. Staging dataset: 48h trace window. Policy uses endpoint tags + span duration floor (only retain spans >10ms with additional reservoir sampling for long traces). Noticed ~10–25% reduction varying by endpoint (higher for small-request endpoints).
- 09:18 - Leah: dashboard usage analytics. Identified panels with <3 views/week that still execute expensive JOIN queries; flagged for removal. Created quick replacement panels using 95th percentile histograms backed by pre-aggregated materialized views.
- 09:26 - Omar: cost telemetry release. Enabled export-batching in the EU exporter; tuned batch size to 1500 events/min to avoid burst throttling.
- 09:34 - Priya: SRE concerns: need to validate sampling doesn't drop root-cause spans for production incidents. Proposed canary policy to preserve all error-level traces and a 1% reservoir of full-traces for every 10k requests.

Detailed experiment notes
1) Adaptive endpoint sampling (Marcus)
- Hypothesis: we can drop low-signal spans at ingestion using endpoint-specific sampling rules and keep errors + slow traces.
- Config: staging policy v0.9 -> rule precedence: error spans (keep), duration>100ms (keep), high-cardinality endpoints rate 1:10, default 1:5 with 1% full-trace reservoir per 10k requests.
- Instrumentation: added temporary debug tag "sampling.v0.9" to trace root; export to internal test index.
- Observations: throughput unchanged; CPU on ingestion nodes reduced by ~7% during bursts; trace-query latency on trimmed dashboards improved 120–180ms median.
- Risk flags: one endpoint (embedder-service) had rare internal errors that only showed up when we sampled aggressively — we reverted sampling to 1:1 for that endpoint and filed JIRA-OBS-4123.

2) Dashboard pruning + replace (Leah)
- Method: computed panel usage from Grafana telemetry for last 60 days; ranked panels by cost (query latency * frequency).
- Actions: removed 14 panels, merged 3 into a single drilldown with time-range variable. Replaced two heavy panels with pre-aggregated series (5m rollups).
- Measurement: expected query-cost savings ~6% for the dashboard tile; observed 4.2% in first 48h while index warm-up continues.

3) Cost telemetry aggregation change (Omar)
- Problem: high-cardinality keys from slow-query traces in EU caused exporter partitioning and higher egress.
- Change: switched to hashed bucketing of query-signature and enabled coarse labels on non-critical keys.
- Result: cardinality down 38% in EU ingest; estimated egress cost savings ~8% for that pipeline.

Operational concerns and mitigations
- Incident retention: SRE wants an immutable pathway for incident traces (all error and any traces attached to PagerDuty incidents should bypass sampling). Action: implement incident-tagged bypass in v1.0. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-10-21.
- Regression risk: sampling tweaks can hide poor-performing code paths. Mitigation: maintain 1% full-trace reservoir across endpoints and add differential alerts when error rates jump without accompanying increased trace density. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-10-19.
- Dashboard discoverability: after pruning, teams reported difficulty finding historical metrics. Mitigation: add a "legacy panels" folder and redirect links. Owner: Leah. ETA: 2026-10-18.

Quick playbook snippets (to be copied to Confluence)
- How to canary sampling policy:
  1) apply policy in staging namespace with debug tag
  2) watch sampling.v0.9 counts in debug index for 24h
  3) validate no drop in error traces (query: timestamp + error && sampling.tag)
  4) roll to canary (1% traffic) then 10% if stable

- Sampler config example (YAML):
  - name: endpoint-priority
    keep_if: span.tags.error == true
    keep_if: span.duration_ms > 100
    default_rate: 0.2
    reservoirs:
      - catch_all: 0.01 # 1% full-trace reservoir per 10k

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we adopt the "hashed bucket" aggregation as default globally? (cost vs. debuggability tradeoff). Vote needed from infra lead.
- Reservoir size: current 1% might be too small for very low-traffic endpoints — consider per-endpoint minimum.
- Dashboard governance: define TTL for "incubation" panels (recommendation: 90 days) before removal.

Action items (owner / due)
- Marcus: implement per-endpoint minimum reservoir logic + unit tests. Due 2026-10-19.
- Leah: finalize dashboard redirect mapping and create legacy folder. Due 2026-10-18.
- Omar: measure EU exporter egress after two weeks and report delta. Due 2026-10-28.
- Priya: implement incident-trace bypass prototype in staging and run incident replay test. Due 2026-10-21.

Notes-to-self / loose fragments
- Quick query for debug index: SELECT count(*) FROM traces WHERE tags.sampling = 'v0.9' GROUP BY service, endpoint; useful for next check.
- Consider adding a lightweight "trace-sampler-preview" page in Console showing expected retention vs. cost for a given endpoint. Product ask potential.

Next meeting: 2026-10-21 (focus = incident bypass test results, reservoir tuning, dashboard redirect roll)

End of notes.
